sewing-machine.definition: A machine that joins fabric and other flexible materials by passing thread through them in linked stitches, usually with one thread above and another below.
sewing-machine.exampleUsage: The sewing machine was used during the activity.

dress-form.definition: A body-shaped stand used by dressmakers and designers to fit, drape, and display garments.
dress-form.exampleUsage: The designer pinned fabric to the dress form.

mannequin.definition: A woman who wears clothes to display fashions.

cutting-table.definition: A large flat worktable used for laying out and cutting fabric or patterns.
cutting-table.exampleUsage: The fabric was spread across the cutting table.

iron.definition: A heavy ductile magnetic metallic element.

serger.definition: A sewing machine that overcasts the raw edges of a fabric with a V-shaped stitch.
serger.exampleUsage: The serger was used during the activity.

embroidery-machine.definition: A sewing machine designed to create decorative stitched designs, often using programmed patterns.
embroidery-machine.exampleUsage: The embroidery machine stitched the logo onto the sample.

pattern-paper.definition: Paper used to draft, copy, or adjust garment patterns.
pattern-paper.exampleUsage: The pattern maker traced the sleeve onto pattern paper.

tailor-s-chalk.definition: A removable marking chalk used to draw temporary lines on fabric.
tailor-s-chalk.exampleUsage: The tailor's chalk marked the seam line.

needle.definition: A slender pointer for indicating the reading on the scale of a measuring instrument.
needle.exampleUsage: The needle was used during the activity.

thread.definition: A long, thin strand used for sewing fabric.

scissors.definition: A gymnastic exercise performed on the pommel horse when the gymnast moves their legs as the blades of scissors move.

pinking-shears.definition: Scissors with zigzag blades used to cut fabric edges in a saw-tooth pattern.
pinking-shears.exampleUsage: Pinking shears created a zigzag edge on the fabric.

seam-ripper.definition: A small tool used to cut and remove unwanted stitches.
seam-ripper.exampleUsage: The seam ripper removed a short line of incorrect stitches.

pin-cushion.definition: A small padded holder used to keep sewing pins and needles safely accessible.
pin-cushion.exampleUsage: Pins were returned to the pin cushion.

measuring-tape.definition: A flexible strip marked with units of length and used for measuring bodies, fabric, or objects.
measuring-tape.exampleUsage: The designer used a measuring tape to record the sleeve length.

thimble.definition: As much as a thimble will hold.

bobbin.definition: A winder around which thread or tape or film or other flexible materials can be wound.

zipper-foot.definition: A narrow sewing-machine presser foot designed to stitch close to a zipper or raised edge.
zipper-foot.exampleUsage: The zipper foot allowed stitching close to the zipper teeth.

sketch.definition: A quick simple drawing showing an idea or subject.

draping.definition: A fashion-design method of arranging and pinning fabric directly on a dress form to develop a garment shape.
draping.exampleUsage: The designer used draping to explore the shape of the skirt.

pattern-making.definition: The process of creating templates used to cut fabric pieces for garments.
pattern-making.exampleUsage: Pattern making turns a design idea into precise garment pieces.

muslin.definition: A plain, lightweight cotton fabric often used to make test garments.

toile.definition: Originally made in France, toile is fabric printed with repeated pastoral or historical scenes, usually in one color on a pale ground.

fitting.definition: A session to check and adjust how clothing sits on a person.

alteration.definition: The act of making something different (as e.g. the size of a garment).

sample.definition: A trial garment made to test a design before production.

production.definition: The act or process of producing something.

fashion-designer.definition: A person who creates concepts and designs for clothing, accessories, or fashion collections.
fashion-designer.exampleUsage: The fashion designer reviewed the fabric samples.

seamstress.definition: A woman who makes or mends dresses.

tailor.definition: To style and tailor in a certain fashion.

pattern-maker.definition: A specialist who creates and adjusts garment patterns from design specifications.
pattern-maker.exampleUsage: The pattern maker converted the sketch into production pieces.

textile-designer.definition: A designer who creates patterns, colors, textures, or structures for fabrics and other textiles.
textile-designer.exampleUsage: The textile designer developed a repeating fabric pattern.

stylist.definition: An artist who is a master of a particular style.

fashion-illustrator.definition: An artist who creates drawings that communicate clothing and fashion ideas.
fashion-illustrator.exampleUsage: The fashion illustrator sketched the new collection.

merchandiser.definition: A businessperson engaged in retail trade.

buyer.definition: A person who chooses products for a store to sell.
